entries.proposition: Text: enzyme activity in mutant cells was markedly reduced compared with wild type, independent of protein expression, so the variant potentially impairs enzyme function rather than protein quantity.
entries.snippet: Importantly, α-Gal A enzymic activity in GLA-MU cells was markedly reduced compared with GLA-WT (figure 4F), and this reduction is independent of protein expression levels.

entries.proposition: Figure 4F as drawn (five points per bar): relative activity about 0.35 for empty vector, about 0.65 for the mutant (ns against empty vector) and about 1.15 for wild type (four stars against both). The mutant's activity is not distinguishable from that of cells carrying no GLA construct; the mutant protein is present at about 1.8 times the empty-vector level (Figure 4C, three stars) with an activity increment over the empty-vector level that is not significant. INFERENZA, reader's: the panel is compatible with a protein that is present and contributes little or no activity above the cells' own background.

entries.proposition: Text: before treatment the mutant to wild-type activity ratio was 37.36 percent; after the chaperone it rose to 45.7 percent, an absolute increase of 8.36 percentage points and a 1.36-fold change.
entries.snippet: This increase was more pronounced in GLA-MU and reached statistical significance (p<0.05). Before drug treatment the ratio of GLA enzymatic activity in MU to WT was 37.36%. After DGJ treatment this ratio increased to 45.7%, representing an absolute increase of 8.36 percentage points and a 1.36-fold change relative to baseline.

entries.proposition: Figure 4G as drawn (five points per bar): wild type about 0.78, wild type with the chaperone about 0.86 (ns); mutant about 0.29, mutant with the chaperone about 0.39 (one star). The absolute activity gain of the mutant is about 0.10 on a scale where wild type is 0.78; the figure has no empty-vector arm, so the gain cannot be separated from a chaperone effect on the host cells' own enzyme (about 0.35 against 1.15 in Figure 4F, i.e. about 30 percent of wild-type level in untransduced-background terms). The threshold figures are those of a published cell-based amenability assay quoted by the authors; that assay was not run here. INFERENZA, reader's.
